  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS = 10.minutes

  included do
    has_many :edits, dependent: :delete_all

    after_update :record_moved_to_trash, if: :was_trashed?
  end

  def edit(leafable_params: {}, leaf_params: {})
    if record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      update_and_record_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    else
      update_without_recording_edit leaf_params, leafable_params
    end
  end

  private
    def record_new_edit?(leafable_params)
      will_change_leafable?(leafable_params) && last_edit_old?
    end

    def last_edit_old?
      edits.empty? || edits.last.created_at.before?(MINIMUM_TIME_BETWEEN_VERSIONS.ago)
    end

    def will_change_leafable?(leafable_params)
      leafable_params.select do |key, value|
        leafable.attributes[key.to_s] != value
      end.present?
    end

    def update_without_recording_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.last&.touch
        update! leaf_params
      end
    end

    def update_and_record_edit(leaf_params, leafable_params)
      transaction do
        new_leafable = dup_leafable_with_attachments leafable
        new_leafable.update!(leafable_params)

        edits.revision.create!(leafable: leafable)
        update! leaf_params.merge(leafable: new_leafable)
      end
    end

    def dup_leafable_with_attachments(leafable)
      leafable.dup.tap do |new|
        leafable.attachment_reflections.each do |name, _|
          new.send(name).attach(leafable.send(name).blob)
        end
      end
    end

    def record_moved_to_trash
      edits.trash.create!(leafable: leafable)
    end

    def was_trashed?
      trashed? && previous_changes.include?(:status)
    end

- The indicator uses `turbo_stream_from leaf, :being_edited`, which is a signed stream name fixed at render time.

- `ApplicationCable::Connection` authenticates by session cookie only, with no per-book check.

require "test_helper"

class ReproScratchTest < ActionCable::Connection::TestCase
  tests ApplicationCable::Connection

  def connect_as(user)
    session = users(user).sessions.start!(user_agent: "test", ip_address: "10.0.0.1")
    cookies.signed[:session_token] = session.token
    connect
    @messages = []
    messages = @messages
    connection.define_singleton_method(:transmit) { |cable_message| messages << cable_message }
    connection
  end

  def subscribe_presence(leaf)
    identifier = { channel: "Turbo::StreamsChannel", signed_stream_name: Turbo::StreamsChannel.signed_stream_name([ leaf, :being_edited ]) }.to_json
    connection.handle_channel_command("command" => "subscribe", "identifier" => identifier)
    connection.subscriptions.identifiers.include?(identifier)
  end

  def wait_for(seconds: 2)
    deadline = Time.now + seconds
    sleep 0.02 until yield || Time.now > deadline
  end

  test "removed editor still receives presence payload" do
    leaf = leaves(:welcome_page)
    connect_as :kevin
    assert subscribe_presence(leaf), "kevin should be subscribed while he has access"

    books(:handbook).accesses.where(user: users(:kevin)).delete_all

    wait_for { @messages.any? { |m| m[:message].to_s.include?("PAYLOAD") } }
    puts "messages seen by removed kevin: #{@messages.inspect}"
    assert_empty @messages.select { |m| m[:message].to_s.include?("PAYLOAD") }
  end
end

# Who is editing a page is only for people who can still edit it.
#
# The editor page subscribes to its "being edited" stream through Turbo::StreamsChannel with a
# signed stream name that stays valid for as long as the page is open. Turbo verifies that
# signature but never checks access, so a collaborator removed from a book keeps receiving the
# payloads, editor names included. Presence streams are therefore authorized when subscribed and
# again for every payload before it is transmitted, so access changes apply to open editors too.
module BeingEditedAuthorization
  STREAM_SUFFIX = ":being_edited"

  private
    def subscribed
      stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params

      if stream_name&.end_with?(STREAM_SUFFIX)
        subscribe_to_being_edited stream_name
      else
        super
      end
    end

    def subscribe_to_being_edited(stream_name)
      leaf = leaf_for_being_edited(stream_name)

      if leaf && can_see_being_edited?(leaf)
        stream_from stream_name, ->(message) { transmit message if can_see_being_edited?(leaf) }
      else
        reject
      end
    end

    def leaf_for_being_edited(stream_name)
      GlobalID::Locator.locate stream_name.delete_suffix(STREAM_SUFFIX), only: Leaf
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      nil
    end

    # Checked on every payload, not just at subscribe time, so removing a collaborator or
    # deactivating a user stops their open subscriptions from receiving presence right away.
    def can_see_being_edited?(leaf)
      user = User.active.find_by(id: connection.current_user&.id)
      user.present? && leaf.book.editable?(user: user)
    end
end

Rails.application.config.to_prepare do
  Turbo::StreamsChannel.prepend BeingEditedAuthorization
end

    assert_not subscription.confirmed?

    broadcast_being_edited_by :david

    broadcast_being_edited_by :david

    broadcast_being_edited_by :david

    broadcast_being_edited_by :david

    assert_equal 1, subscription.payloads.size
  end

    assert subscription.rejected?
    assert_not subscription.confirmed?

# Who is editing a page is only for people who can still edit it.
#
# The editor page subscribes to its "being edited" stream through Turbo::StreamsChannel with a
# signed stream name that stays valid for as long as the page is open. Turbo verifies that
# signature but never checks access, so a collaborator removed from a book keeps receiving the
# payloads, editor names included. Presence streams are therefore authorized when subscribed and
# again for every payload before it is transmitted, so access changes apply to open editors too.
module BeingEditedAuthorization
  STREAM_SUFFIX = ":being_edited"

  private
    def subscribed
      stream_name = verified_stream_name_from_params

      if stream_name&.end_with?(STREAM_SUFFIX)
        subscribe_to_being_edited stream_name
      else
        super
      end
    end

    def subscribe_to_being_edited(stream_name)
      leaf = leaf_for_being_edited(stream_name)

      if leaf && can_see_being_edited?(leaf)
        stream_from stream_name, ->(message) { transmit message if can_see_being_edited?(leaf) }
      else
        reject
      end
    end

    def leaf_for_being_edited(stream_name)
      GlobalID::Locator.locate stream_name.delete_suffix(STREAM_SUFFIX), only: Leaf
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      nil
    end

    # Checked on every payload, not just at subscribe time, so removing a collaborator or
    # deactivating a user stops their open subscriptions from receiving presence right away.
    def can_see_being_edited?(leaf)
      user = User.active.find_by(id: connection.current_user&.id)
      user.present? && leaf.book.editable?(user: user)
    end
end

## Summary

**Root cause.** The editor page subscribes to its presence stream through `Turbo::StreamsChannel` with a signed stream name. Turbo only checks that the signature is valid. It never checks access, and the subscription lasts as long as the page is open. A collaborator removed from the book therefore kept receiving every "being edited" payload, editor names included. Anyone holding that signed name could also subscribe to it directly.

**Fix.** `lib/rails_ext/being_edited_authorization.rb` prepends a module onto `Turbo::StreamsChannel`. For `:being_edited` streams only:
- **On subscribe**, the leaf must exist and its book must be editable by the connected user. Otherwise the subscription is rejected.
- **On every payload**, the same check runs again before anything is transmitted. Revoking access or deactivating a user takes effect on open editors immediately.

Other streams are untouched. The view, the broadcast, and the signed names are unchanged, so pages that are already open keep working and the indicator still appears for editors and administrators.

I did not use a dedicated channel: pages opened before the deploy still subscribe through `Turbo::StreamsChannel`, so the gate has to live there.

**Tradeoffs:**
- Each payload costs one user lookup and one access lookup per subscriber.
- Deactivated users are also cut off. This goes slightly beyond the literal request, but a deactivated user's socket would otherwise keep receiving payloads.
- The gate matches the `:being_edited` suffix, which the view and controller also spell out. An integration test covers the full path, so a rename would fail a test rather than silently reopen the leak.

**Verification.**
- I added 15 tests. Eight of them fail without the fix, including the end-to-end scenario where a removed collaborator's open editor is still subscribed.
- The tests that pass both with and without the fix check that editors, administrators, and the save-time broadcast still work.
- RuboCop reports no offenses on the changed files.
- The production eager-load and Zeitwerk checks pass.

I did not run the browser system tests, so the client-side behavior was verified only through the server-side channel and integration tests.
